title: Synchronous Buck Converter
subtitle: 6.622 Power Electronics Design Project
blurb: A 160 W, 12 V synchronous buck whose component values were chosen by a Python optimizer sweeping MOSFETs, magnetics, and capacitors for maximum efficiency.
description: Designed a synchronous buck converter (40 V → 12 V, 160 W) for a solar-car-style application where efficiency matters and cost does not. Given a list of components, a Python script swept all 16 high-side/low-side MOSFET pairings plus magnetics and capacitor banks against a full loss model to find the most efficient design.

The optimized design reaches 97.8% worst-case efficiency — efficient enough that the MOSFETs dissipate little enough power to run with no heatsink. Closed-loop transient behavior was verified with an averaged LTSpice model and a PI compensator.
highlights: Python design sweep over 16 MOSFET pairs, RM-core magnetics, and capacitor banks against conduction, switching, gate-drive, Coss, and reverse-recovery loss models.
Synchronous rectification chosen over a Schottky diode, saving ~4.9 W of low-side loss.
Averaged LTSpice model with an LT1001 PI compensator validating ±120 W load transients.
Inductor sized for 0.267 T peak flux (1.12× saturation margin) with full thermal analysis.

title: High-Frequency GaN Characterization
subtitle: MIT RLE · IEEE APEC 2026
blurb: Measurement method and comprehensive data for Coss loss and dynamic RdsON in commercial GaN devices at switching frequencies up to 30 MHz.
description: Adapted a resonant, Class-E-style measurement circuit to extract both output-capacitance (Coss) loss and dynamic on-resistance in commercial 650 V GaN devices at frequencies up to 30 MHz — a regime where conventional loss estimation breaks down.

A three-configuration power-difference method separates Coss and conduction losses by keeping circulating current constant across tests. I built an automated SCPI test platform that tunes for zero-voltage switching, logs data to the cloud, and tracks operating points across 162 test runs per device.
highlights: Co-authored paper accepted to the 2026 IEEE Applied Power Electronics Conference (APEC); to appear in IEEE Xplore.
Custom high-frequency boards on Rogers 4350B with copper-tube and single-turn foil resonant inductors.
SCPI automation that locates the ZVS minimum-input-power point and logs voltage, frequency, and current per run.
Established intra-family Coss scaling trends and temperature dependence across manufacturers.

title: Differential Amplifier IC
subtitle: Fabricated by Intel · 22nm
blurb: A CMOS differential amplifier designed, laid out, and verified in Intel's 22nm PDK, then integrated into a shared-bus IC and submitted DRC/LVS-clean.
description: Designed a CMOS differential amplifier in the Intel 22nm PDK, tuning transistor sizing and biasing to maximize a gain/swing/power figure of merit. Verified gain, output swing, power, and node voltages in Cadence.

Also implemented the supporting cells — inverter, pass gate, and a digital code checker — for integration into a shared-bus IC architecture, and delivered a full-system layout that passed DRC and LVS cleanly. The design was fabricated by Intel.
highlights: Full custom flow in Cadence: schematic, layout, and verification.
Inverter, pass gate, and digital code checker implemented for shared-bus integration.
DRC/LVS-clean submission of both individual cells and the full system.
Fabricated on real silicon by Intel.

title: 32-bit RISC-V Processor
subtitle: 5-stage pipelined CPU
blurb: A 32-bit, 5-stage pipelined RISC-V processor with caching, branch prediction, and full bypassing.
description: Designed and implemented a 32-bit RISC-V 5-stage pipelined processor with a 600 ns critical path. Integrated a 32-bit direct-mapped cache and a 2-way set-associative cache to improve memory performance.
Optimized throughput with branch prediction and full bypassing from the writeback and execute stages to resolve data hazards without stalling.
highlights: Direct-mapped and 2-way set-associative caches.
Branch prediction to reduce control-hazard penalties.
Full bypassing from writeback and execute stages.

title: Go-Kart Motor Drive
subtitle: PWM H-bridge power stage
blurb: A discrete PWM motor drive built from a 555 timer and comparator, driving a 1.5 HP motor at 36 V / 30 A.
description: Built a PWM signal generator with adjustable duty cycle and frequency using a 555 timer and an LM311 comparator, then added delay circuitry to safely drive two N-channel MOSFETs in a totem-pole configuration.
The drive handled 36 V and 30 A, successfully running a 1.5 HP go-kart motor — a hands-on exercise in component selection, cost, and high-power switching.
highlights: Adjustable-duty PWM from a 555 timer + LM311 comparator.
Dead-time / delay circuitry for safe totem-pole switching.
Discrete N-channel MOSFET power stage.

title: Motorized Window Shade
subtitle: 6.1311 Independent Inquiry
blurb: A battery-powered, wirelessly controlled skylight shade with custom buck converters, an H-bridge, and 3D-printed gear trains.
description: Designed a battery-powered motorized shade for an inaccessible, slanted skylight. The system runs from two series 9 V batteries (14.4–19.2 V) and uses an ESP32-C3 for wireless control, an H-bridge motor drive with IR2125 gate drivers, and two feedback buck converters (18 V → 5 V and 18 V → 12 V).

Added a comparator + Zener low-voltage protection circuit and 10-turn potentiometer position feedback. For the mechanical side I learned CAD and 3D-printed 60:1 and 125:1 gear trains to couple the motor to the roller and the position sensor.
highlights: Two feedback-regulated buck converters plus low-voltage protection.
H-bridge motor drive with IR2125 high/low-side gate drivers.
Self-taught CAD and 3D-printed gear trains and couplings.

title: YouTube / Panopto Downloader
subtitle: Chrome extension + local server
blurb: A Chrome extension and Flask server that downloads and composites multi-stream lecture and YouTube videos with ffmpeg.
description: Built a Chrome extension backed by a local Flask server to download YouTube and Panopto videos. For Panopto lectures it detects multiple camera/slide streams and offers picture-in-picture, side-by-side, or single-stream modes.

PiP and side-by-side modes download each stream separately and composite them with ffmpeg automatically. The server caches browser cookies and exposes a system-check panel for yt-dlp, ffmpeg, and the JS runtime dependencies.
highlights: Multi-stream Panopto detection with PiP and side-by-side compositing.
Flask server with cookie caching and a dependency system-check panel.
Download button injected directly into the YouTube UI.

title: YouTube Botnet Detection
subtitle: Coordination-detection pipeline
blurb: An educational toolkit that extracts 80+ behavioral, text, temporal, and network features from YouTube comments to detect coordinated botnets.
description: Built a research pipeline that collects YouTube comments via the Data API and extracts 80+ temporal, text/NLP, network, behavioral, and semantic features. Two detection paths are available: a semantic + temporal coordination detector (BotBuster) and a feature-based HDBSCAN/DBSCAN clustering ensemble.
The system stores data in SQLite, produces Plotly/Matplotlib HTML reports, and ships a Flask API that powers a companion Chrome extension and batch analysis endpoint.
highlights: Temporal, text, network co-occurrence, behavioral, and semantic feature extractors.
Coordination-graph clustering plus an HDBSCAN/DBSCAN ensemble.
SQLite storage, HTML visual reports, and a Flask API for the extension.

title: Multiplayer Snake on FPGA
subtitle: Two-FPGA client/host game
blurb: A multiplayer Snake game built in Verilog on FPGAs — a client/host split with HDMI video out, a hardware math accelerator, and joystick control.
description: Designed a multiplayer Snake game in Verilog on RealDigital Urbana FPGA boards, split into a host and client that communicate over a bus. The host runs the game loop — polling joystick inputs, advancing each player's snake, and enforcing the rules — while the client renders the playfield.

Snake and apple positions live in on-chip and external memory; rendering streams from a frame buffer through TMDS encoders to an HDMI display, and a hardware math accelerator handles per-player head and tail movement.

title: Hand-Wound Brushless Motor
subtitle: From-scratch motor build
blurb: A brushless motor built from scratch — hand-wound copper coils on 3D-printed mounts spinning a magnet rotor under electronic commutation.
description: Built a brushless motor by hand: wound copper coils onto 3D-printed mounts arranged around a central magnet rotor on an acrylic base, then energized the coils in sequence with a microcontroller to spin it up.
A hands-on exercise in electromagnetics, coil winding, and commutation timing.

title: Induction Motor Build
subtitle: Hand-built rotor & frame
blurb: A hand-built induction motor — wound coils mounted in a custom frame and spun up under power as a working demo.
description: Built an induction motor largely from scratch, mounting hand-wound coils and a rotor in a custom frame and powering it up to spin as a demonstration.
A hands-on study of rotating magnetic fields and electromechanical energy conversion.
